step1_figure.description: A bootstrapped clock driver circuit that uses cross-coupled NMOS transistors and capacitors to generate a pulsed output voltage roughly twice the supply voltage (2*VDD) to fully turn on NMOS switches without suffering a threshold voltage drop.

v_out_high.description: Maximum high voltage level of the output clock signal.

source.reference: Text: 'The output of the driver circuit then goes to 2VDD'

equation.explanation: The output is pulled to node B, which is bootstrapped to twice the supply voltage when the input goes high.
equation.assumptions: Negligible charge sharing losses with parasitic capacitances and ideal precharging of node B.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Ideal is 3.6V. In practice, parasitic capacitances at node B and the output node will reduce the peak voltage slightly through charge sharing.

v_boot_b.description: Bootstrapped peak voltage at node B.

equation.explanation: Node B is precharged to VDD by M2 and then boosted by an additional VDD when INV2 output goes high.
equation.assumptions: C2 (1000fF) is much larger than the parasitic capacitance at node B.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Ideal is 3.6V, reduced slightly by parasitics. C2 is large (1pF), so the boost efficiency should be high.

v_boot_a.description: Bootstrapped peak voltage at node A.

equation.explanation: Node A is precharged to VDD by M1 and then boosted by an additional VDD when INV1 output goes high.
equation.assumptions: C1 (100fF) is much larger than the parasitic capacitance at node A.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Ideal is 3.6V. C1 is smaller (100fF), so charge sharing with M2's gate capacitance will cause a slightly larger voltage drop compared to node B.

t_rise.description: Rise time of the output clock signal, dependent on load capacitance.

source.reference: Text: 'characterize the performance as a function of the load capacitance.'

equation.explanation: The rise time is determined by the ability of the PMOS (M4) to charge the load capacitance from the bootstrapped node B.
equation.assumptions: Constant average drive current during the transition.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Estimated based on typical 130nm drive strengths for a 10um device driving a 1pF load.

power.description: Average power consumption of the clock driver.

source.reference: Text: 'minimize layout area and power (the charging and discharging of the parasitic capacitors doesn't waste power)'

equation.explanation: Dynamic power consumed by switching the capacitors (C1, C2) and the load capacitance.
equation.assumptions: Measured over an integer number of clock cycles.

sky130_expected.calculation: P \approx f \cdot C_{total} \cdot V^2. C_{total} \approx 2.1pF. At 25MHz, P \approx 25e6 * 2.1e-12 * (3.6)^2 \approx 680\mu W.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Dynamic power dominates and is heavily dependent on the input clock frequency and load capacitance.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure bootstrapped voltages at nodes A and B, output high voltage, rise time, and average power consumption.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Charge-pump clock driver testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Define parameters for the parameterized netlist
.param W_xm1i=2u L_xm1i=0.15u
.param W_xm2i=4u L_xm2i=0.15u
.param W_xm1a=4u L_xm1a=0.15u
.param W_xm2a=8u L_xm2a=0.15u
.param W_xm1=2u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=10u L_xm2=0.15u
.param W_xm3=10u L_xm3=0.15u
.param W_xm4=10u L_xm4=0.15u

* Input clock (25MHz)
Vclk N003 0 PULSE(0 1.8 0 100p 100p 20n 40n)

* --- DUT START ---
xm1i N001 N003 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1i} l={L_xm1i}
VDD VDD 0 1.8
xm2i N001 N003 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2i} l={L_xm2i}
Cload Vout 0 1e-12
C2 N002 B 1e-12
xm1a N002 N001 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1a} l={L_xm1a}
xm2a N002 N001 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2a} l={L_xm2a}
xm3 Vout N001 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
xm4 Vout N001 B B sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
C1 N001 A 1e-13
xm2 B A VDD 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
xm1 A B VDD 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
* --- DUT END ---

* Initial conditions to help startup
.ic v(vout)=0 v(a)=1.8 v(b)=1.8

.control
tran 100p 200n

* Measure steady state boosted voltages (after a few cycles)
meas tran v_out_high max v(vout) from=100n to=200n
meas tran v_boot_b max v(b) from=100n to=200n
meas tran v_boot_a max v(a) from=100n to=200n

* Measure rise time on a later edge (10% to 90% of expected 3.6V swing)
meas tran t_rise trig v(vout) val=0.36 rise=4 targ v(vout) val=3.24 rise=4

* Measure average power from VDD
meas tran pwr_integ integ i(VDD) from=100n to=200n
let power = -(pwr_integ / 100n) * 1.8

print v_out_high v_boot_b v_boot_a t_rise power
quit
.endc
